document.title: Afghanistan: Taliban Convene Ulema, Iran and Bin Ladin on the Agenda
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] The upcoming Taliban Ulema will discuss Iran and Bin Laden's presence in Afghanistan. The source sees a divide in Taliban ranks but expects the Ulema to reiterate Mullah Omar's position that Bin Laden is a guest and not proven involved in any bombings.

events.description: Taliban convened a large ulema gathering in Kandahar that anointed Mullah Omar Amir ul-Momimin.
Ulema gathering in Kabul began, meeting Sept 21-22 with plans for a third day Sept 23, to discuss Iran and Bin Ladin.
Radio Shariat announced the five questions for the ulema.
Taliban-convened ulema gathering (about 1,500 per reports; 5,000 per Gailani) began in Kabul, invited by Rabbani; met Sept 21-22 with a third day planned Sept 23.
Radio Shariat announced the ulema's five questions on Iran and Taliban legitimacy.
Political officer phone conversation about ulema attendance, including possible Hazaras.
Source briefed Peshawar political officer on Radio Shariat's ulema agenda; Islamabad cable 7186 sent.
Taliban convened large ulema gathering in Kandahar that anointed Mullah Omar 'Amir ul-Mominin'.
State Department relayed Islamabad cable 7186 to Under Secretary Pickering.

key_claims: Taliban convened roughly 1,500 handpicked ulema in Kabul in September 1998 to discuss Iran, Bin Ladin and Taliban legitimacy.
The meeting was largely an orchestrated show of allegiance to Mullah Omar, especially from northern ulema.
The Taliban leadership was reportedly split over Bin Ladin, with Rabbani opposing his presence and Omar favoring keeping him.
The ulema were expected to let Bin Ladin stay with strictly curtailed political activity.
A fatwa justifying war against Iran if it invaded Afghanistan was expected.
